_about: karma's reads on players that the numbers can't see. Kept by hand. 'motor': high-intensity player whose output rises with his minutes; never take an under on him when a starter at his position is out. 'small_ball_5': plays centre in small lineups, so there is rebound upside when the bigs sit. 'primary_guard_defender': guards the opponent's main ball-handler, so his minutes hold up whatever happens to his shooting. 'rebounds_suppressed_with_giannis': fade this player's rebound overs when Giannis plays. 'low_mistake_trusted': the coach trusts him and his minutes are steady, but his output moves between stats, so prefer combo props. 'big_game_closer': plays more and is on the floor at the end of close or big games. Team tag 'trapping_defense' (karma, 8 Nov): good defences come in two styles. TRAPPING (DET, TOR, CLE lately, OKC historically) forces turnovers by pressuring the playmaker; CONTAINING (SAS, current OKC) contests and stays home and forces few. Only trapping moves playmakers' TOV/AST props. Tag 'rim_assists' (karma, 8 Nov): about half or more of his assists are dunks/layups, so his assist props depend less on teammates' shooting than a kick-out passer's.

OKC.note: karma, 7 Nov: with SGA and whoever else, OKC know how to win; they have won through constant lineup changes for two seasons. Measured (SGA's game logs): with SGA playing and one of Holmgren / J. Williams missing, 38-7 in 2024-25 and 40-5 in 2025-26; with both missing 5-0 and 5-1 (3-2 so far in 2026-27). So do not let our absence penalty sink OKC's team total/margin the way it would for a normal team; their system holds. Example (karma, verified in game logs): 9 Mar 2026 v DEN, OKC beat Jokic's Nuggets without J. Williams, Holmgren, Caruso AND Hartenstein; SGA 35/9/15 with 0 TO, tying Wilt's 126 straight 20-point games. Thunder Collective (6 Nov): Caruso back; new pieces Micah Peavy (POA defender) and Dalen Terry; Jaylin Williams out (back spasms). OKC lack wing size, so Cam Boozer could give them problems; Mara likely draws Edey/Boozer. Reporters expect a close OKC win at MEM with SGA closing (MEM's only closer is Jerome). Next: WAS on the 2nd night of a back-to-back (Caruso may rest), then POR twice in Portland. Hoop Collective (7 Nov): OKC lost three all-defensive players (Holmgren 8-10 weeks, Wallace, J. Williams); their defence was their offence (1st in points off turnovers each of the last 3 seasons) but they are about 22nd in the 6 games since. So SGA now works against set half-court defences loaded up on him; teams make Ajay Mitchell beat them. Discount OKC's season turnover/fast-break numbers in game_lens. karma, 7 Nov: the short-handed group is LEARNING to play together, so season-to-date stats since the injuries understate them. Example: ranked ~22nd in forcing turnovers since the injuries, then 17 pts off turnovers by halftime at MEM (7 Nov). Weight their most recent games over the post-injury average. karma, 8 Nov: OKC started Hartenstein + Aday Mara together (McCain to bench) vs WAS without AD: 'for a good start and collecting data points with the double-big lineup'. Treat early double-big games as experiments: track minutes together, rebound margin and +/- before it changes Hartenstein REB / Mara / McCain props. 8 Nov vs WAS: 3rd straight opponent held to a season-low FG% (WAS 30%, OKC by 39). Double big result: Hartenstein 14 reb in 18 min, Mara 18p 8r in 27 min. karma: when Chet returns, Hartenstein's role holds (9.2 reb with Chet in 2025-26 vs 10.1 without), Mara keeps developmental minutes, and Hartenstein/Chet foul trouble gives Mara a significant role (a live-bet spot vs foul-drawing bigs). karma, 8 Nov: be careful picking props in OKC games. Overs on OKC's OPPONENTS only when that team has what beats them (shot creators who score without turnovers, a middle game, size that rebounds). Held 3 straight opponents to season-low FG%. karma, 8 Nov: OKC's passing-lane scheme (Wallace, J-Dub, Caruso) led the league in forced TOV in 2024-25 and 2025-26 (15.7/g both). 2026-27 fell to 21st (14.0): 26 Oct-4 Nov only 7-12 forced, 3-8 steals; last two (MEM 18 forced/10 stl, WAS 11/9 stl) show it returning. Check whether the dip lines up with Caruso's absence. karma, 8 Nov: that turnover edge is why OKC blow teams out: they force turnovers on opposing guards while SGA is one of the least turnover-prone high-usage guards (measured: 3rd-lowest TOV rate of the top-20 usage players in 2026-27, 2.2/g; 2nd in 2025-26). OKC TOV margin +3.8/g in 2025-26 (1st), +2.0 in 2026-27 (7th) so far. karma, 8 Nov (rotation pattern): Daigneault plays the starters ~5 min, then subs out Hartenstein, Chet, Ajay Mitchell and J-Dub; Shai plays on with defenders/rookies and one backup big (Jaylin Williams) and holds or builds the lead. Early 2nd half, when opponents rest their best 5 and bring in their bench, OKC sends out J-Dub, Ajay, Hartenstein and McCain (two-way 'demons') against that bench; if they extend the lead until Shai and Chet return, the blowout starts. Big-type flexibility (Mara roller, Hart hub, Chet all-around, J-Dub at the 5) doesn't dent Shai's output; the big's prop follows his role that night (Hart hub = AST/+-, low PTS). TESTED 8 Nov (ESPN play-by-play, lineups rebuilt from subs; games Shai started). 2025-26 (68 g): Shai + bench (none of Chet/J-Dub/Hart/Ajay) 404 min, +11.2/48; Shai + 1-2 core +17.1; Shai + 3-4 core +19.3; no Shai but 2+ of J-Dub/Ajay/Hart/Chet/McCain 661 min +10.6 (vs opp bench +9.6, vs opp starters +11.5); no Shai and <2 of them -3.0. With opp starters mostly off: Shai on +23.3/48 (638 min), off +6.1. Net by quarter +4.6/+2.9/+3.3/+2.1 (margin 4.6, 7.4, 10.7, 13.1): the lead builds steadily. Core starters' first Q1 sub ~6-7.5 min in; Shai subbed in Q1 in only 22 of 68 games, so his rest is mostly early Q2/Q4. 2026-27 (10 g): Shai + bench +11.8; no-Shai 'demons' unit only +2.1 (vs opp bench -3.0, 63 min) so far; quarters +2.6/+5.6/-0.3/+0.3. Prop read: the most lopsided stretch is Shai vs opponents' bench, so fade opposing bench players' overs vs OKC. [ThreeCone (YouTube), 8 Nov 2026] OUT: Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren (back ~new year, maybe Feb), Cason Wallace (all three went down vs LAC). Wiggins, Isaiah Joe, Dort traded. OKC 8-2, 2nd-best defence, top-10 net rating, 4 straight wins. Easy schedule ahead (POR x2, SAC, BKN). CORRECTION to the 2026-27 rotation numbers: the 'no-Shai demons' unit this season is mostly Ajay/Hart/McCain (J-Dub out), not J-Dub.

DET.note: karma, 8 Nov: trapping defence: pressure the handler, make him pass in distress, help defenders jump the lanes. Forces 17.1 TOV/g (4th, league 15.1). Ausar Thompson/Kris Dunn-type point-of-attack pressure. Lean to opposing playmakers' TURNOVER overs; be wary of their assist overs. karma, 8 Nov: the trap does NOT work on SGA. vs DET: 48 pts on 17/26, 2 TOV (15 Mar 2025, Ausar 21 min); 47 on 12/19, 21/25 FT, 4 TOV, Ausar FOULED OUT (6 PF, 26 min) (30 Mar 2026); 33 pts, 1 TOV (2 Apr 2025). Elite, low-turnover handlers punish the pressure with free throws and Ausar foul trouble; it only bites turnover-prone handlers (Luka, Reaves, LeBron). UPDATE 9 Nov (LAL@DET, Luka out): DET did NOT trap Reaves early; they played him one-on-one with light help (karma, watching). Reaves 43 pts, 11/11 FT, 1 TOV in 37 min; DET trapped him only late, after 30+. Read: the trap is for the opponent's star; a stand-in creator (star out) gets single coverage, so his usage bump goes straight into points. Don't apply trapping_defense to a stand-in lead handler.
